policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'neither is it for us to put any man to death' renders first-person plural לָנוּ (qere); ketiv לי would be 'for me'. The alternative_rendering note ('for us shalt thou') keeps 'us' and does not decide.
ASV 'let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us' is a passive that renders hophal יֻתַּן (qere) and niphal ינתן (ketiv) alike; no note is mapped. Base qere retained.
ASV 'they fell all seven together' renders 'the seven of them' שְׁבַעְתָּם (qere); ketiv שבעתים 'sevenfold' is not what the English says.
וְהֵמָּה (qere) and והם (ketiv) are spelling forms of the same pronoun; ASV 'And they were put to death' renders either. Base qere retained.

ASV 'at the beginning of barley harvest' needs an English preposition whether the Hebrew has בִּתְחִלַּת (qere) or an adverbial construct תחלת (ketiv); the wording does not distinguish. Base qere retained.

תְּלָאוּם (qere) and תלום (ketiv) are orthographic forms of the same verb 'hanged them'; ASV 'had hanged them' renders either. The 'broad place' note is alternative_rendering on a different word. Base qere retained.

The readings differ only in שָׁמָּה/שם and the presence of the article on פלשתים; ASV 'where the Philistines' uses the English definite article with the people-name regardless, so it does not distinguish. Base qere retained.
ASV 'and Ishbi-benob, who was of the sons of the giant' renders the proper name וְיִשְׁבִּי (qere); ketiv וישבו 'and they dwelt' has no counterpart in the English.

ASV 'a man of great stature' is compatible with both מָדוֹן (qere) and מדין (ketiv, 'measures', cf. 1 Chr 20:6 sense); the English chooses neither. The Raphah note is a hebrew_gloss on 'giant'. Base qere retained.

ASV 'Jonathan the son of Shimei' transliterates the ketiv שמעי (Shimei); qere שִׁמְעָה would be 'Shimeah/Shimea'. The 'other' note contrasting 'In 1 Chr. 2:13; 20:7, Shimea' confirms the ASV text here is the ketiv form.
